proof_summary: Writing the rank as \(n+\lfloor e^{H_n}-1\rfloor\), the proof shows for \(n\ge5\) that \(1<e^{H_{n+1}}-e^{H_n}<2\), so the floor rises by one or two (with the initial cases handled by direct exponential bounds). Telescoping gives \(\#3=F(N+1)-N-1\) and \(\#2=2N+1-F(N+1)\), where \(F(n)=\lfloor e^{H_n}-1\rfloor\); since \(F(n)/n\to e^\gamma\), the ratio tends to \((e^\gamma-1)/(2-e^\gamma)\), and monotone harmonic-error bounds evaluated at \(n=7\), together with exponential-series estimates, give \(16/9<e^\gamma<41/23\), placing this limit between \(3.5\) and \(3.6\).
